name: Azpieuskalki model improvement via Nafarroa town CSV fix

description: Add 53 Nafarroa towns to CSV + fix hyphen normalization + disable validation filter → 10 classes, 37K sentences, acc 51.02% (was 49.76% on 410 samples). ipar-goi-nafarrera now has 5.8K sentences (was 18). hego-goi-nafarrera still 0 — towns not scraped yet.

asi.hypothesis: Fixing Nafarroa town CSV gap and hyphen matching would unlock new data for azpieuskalki training
asi.result: ipar-goi-nafarrera grew from 18 to 5842 sentences. Overall acc went 49.76% → 51.02% but test set grew 13x. hego-goi-nafarrera still 0 samples — towns are in CSV but were never scraped.
asi.next: Scrape high-value Nafarroa towns (>50 passages) to get hego-goi-nafarrera data; then investigate sartaldekoa/sartaldeko-naf-lap confusion

description: Scrape 28 Nafarroa hego-goi-nafarrera towns (180 passages merged → 2343 total). First time all 11 classes have training data. hego-goi-nafarrera at 80.71% (best!) but overall acc dropped to 50.06% (11 classes harder). Confusion matrix: sartaldekoa→debagoiena(160), sartaldeko-naf-lap→beterri(165) — dialect continuum.

asi.hypothesis: Scraping Nafarroa hego-goi-nafarrera towns would provide missing class data
asi.result: hego-goi-nafarrera: 4497 sentences, 80.71% — best class. Overall 50.06% (down from 51.02% on 10 classes).
asi.ceiling_hypothesis: Dialect continuum limits: neighboring azpieuskalkiak share lexicon, capping at ~55%
asi.next: Try class balancing (oversampling weak classes) and hyperparameter sweep

description: Class balancing with oversample_factor=3: oversampled 2 minority classes, downsampled 9 majority classes. 25.73% — much worse. Oversampling reinforces noise in small classes; minority classes (sartaldekoa 2.28%, sartaldeko-naf-lap 0.55%) collapsed.

asi.hypothesis: Class balancing via oversampling would help weak classes
asi.result: 25.73% — much worse than 50.06%. sartaldekoa collapsed to 2.28%, sartaldeko-naf-lap to 0.55%. Oversampling noise hurts more than imbalance.
asi.rollback_reason: Oversampling reinforced noise in minority classes instead of improving them
asi.next_action_hint: Try hyperparameter tuning (larger dim, more wordNgrams, different lr) without oversampling

description: Label verification audit: chain clean (0 unmapped, 0 missing regions). Key findings: ipar-goi-nafarrera data comes from Gipuzkoan border towns (errenteria, hondarribia, oiartzun) rather than Nafarroa proper. hego-goi-nafarrera mixes Zaraitzu/Erronkari/Aezkoa with Sakana. This is a reasonable 2-way simplification of Wikipedia's 4-5 Nafarroan azpieuskalkiak.

asi.hypothesis: Verify labeling chain matches Wikipedia/Ahotsak classification
asi.result: Chain is clean. Our 2-way split (ipar/hego) simplifies Wikipedia's 4-5 Nafarroan azpieuskalkiak. ipar-goi data dominated by Gipuzkoan border towns, not true Nafarroan towns. hego-goi mixes Zaraitzu/Erronkari (ekialdeko nafarrera) with Sakana.
asi.key_issue: ipar-goi-nafarrera trained on Gipuzkoan transitional towns → likely explains beterri↔ipar confusion
asi.next: Consider splitting nafar azpieuskalkiak into 3: mendebalekoa (Bortziriak/Baztan), iparraldekoa (Ultzamaldea), hegoaldekoa (Sakana+Erronkari). But data is scarce for finer splits.

description: dim=100, epoch=100, lr=0.5, wordNgrams=2, autotune 180s: 50.62% (was 50.06%). +0.56% marginal improvement. sartaldekoa 11.62%, sartaldeko-naf-lap 10.44%, zuberera 2.06% still very weak.

asi.hypothesis: Lower dim + longer autotune would improve generalization for 11 classes
asi.result: 50.62% vs 50.06% — within noise floor. sartaldekoa 9.11→11.62%, sartaldeko-naf-lap 9.07→10.44%. zuberera unchanged at 2.06%.
asi.rollback_reason: Margin below noise floor (0.56% on 11-class problem). Not keeping a 0.6% improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Try removing Gipuzkoan transitional towns from ipar-goi-nafarrera; or try minCount=2 filtering rare n-grams

description: Ahotsak-aligned classification: scraped official town→azpieuskalki assignments from Ahotsak.eus, fixed 68 CSV mismatches. 15 classes with min_samples=500 → 11 active, 63.84% (up from 50.06%). mendebal-sortaldea 86.71%, erdialde-sartaldea 76.88%. 4 classes collapsed due to small sample size.

asi.hypothesis: Using official Ahotsak town→azpieuskalki assignments would fix labeling errors and improve accuracy
asi.result: 63.84% (was 50.06%) — +13.7pp improvement. 68 mismatches fixed (Deba valley, Urola coast, Leitzaldea, Bidasoa, Baztan, Zuberoa assignments).
asi.collapsed: erdialde-erdigunea 0%, nafar-hego-sartaldea 0%, ekialde-nafarra 0%, mendebal-sartaldea 0% — too few test samples
asi.next: Try min_samples=200 to keep more classes; consider merging sibling classes that have <300 training samples

description: Ahotsak-aligned classification final: 10 classes (min=400), 68.32% accuracy. Core classes (Mendebal-sortaldea 87%, Erdialde-sartaldea 79%) very strong. Fixed 68 town mismatches from official Ahotsak data. Collapsed small Ahotsak classes (tartekoa, erdigunekoa, basaburua, erdigunekoa-nl, baztangoa) into siblings.

asi.hypothesis: Final Ahotsak-aligned classification with merged small classes
asi.result: 68.32% on 10 classes. mendebal-sortaldea 87.02%, erdialde-sartaldea 78.60%, erdialde-sortaldea 62.10%, nafar-sortaldea 53.56%. Weak: west-Bizkaian (0%), Sakana (1%), Labourdin (0%), Ekialde-nafarra (0%).
asi.classification_scheme: 10 classes derived from Ahotsak 18 azpieuskalkiak via merging small classes
asi.remaining_issues: Small classes (<500 samples) collapse — need more data or data augmentation
asi.verdict: Ahotsak-aligned classification is correct and improves accuracy by 18pp over original custom scheme

description: Hyperparameter: dim=300, autotune 300s (was dim=200, 60s). 67.68% (was 68.32%). Marginal regression — bigger model doesn't help when bottleneck is class imbalance. Small classes still collapse.

asi.hypothesis: Larger dim (300) + longer autotune (300s) would improve accuracy
asi.result: 67.68% (was 68.32%) — regression. Extra capacity overfits large classes.
asi.rollback_reason: Bigger model overfits dominant classes instead of helping small ones
asi.next_action_hint: Try loss=hs (hierarchical softmax) to address class imbalance. Or try wordNgrams=3 for longer lexical patterns.

description: Hierarchical softmax (loss='hs'): 68.02% (was 68.32%). Tradeoff: small classes dramatically improved (0%→30-47%), but Bizkaian dropped 10pp. Mendebal-sartaldea 30%, Naflap-sartaldea 46%, Ekialde-nafarra 42% — all non-zero for first time. Overall tied with ns.

asi.hypothesis: Hierarchical softmax would help collapsed small classes by not sampling negatives
asi.result: 68.02% (was 68.32%) — essentially tied. Small classes revived (0%→30-47%), but dominant Bizkaian dropped 10pp.
asi.rollback_reason: Overall metric not improved. HS trades large-class accuracy for small-class accuracy.
asi.next_action_hint: Try hs with dim=300 to see if larger capacity preserves big-class accuracy while keeping small-class gains. Or try hs with longer autotune.

description: HS loss + dim=300 + epoch=50: 68.14%. Marginal improvement over hs+dim=200 (68.02%) but still below ns baseline (68.32%). Larger capacity doesn't recover the big-class accuracy loss from HS.

asi.hypothesis: HS with larger capacity (dim=300, epoch=50) would preserve large-class accuracy while keeping small-class gains
asi.result: 68.14% — HS fundamentially trades big-class for small-class accuracy. Larger dim doesn't fix this.
asi.next_action_hint: Try wordNgrams=3 for longer lexical patterns. Or try combining ns with minCount=2 to filter noise in small classes.

description: wordNgrams=3: 64.09% (was 68.32%). Trigram features overfit large classes — all 7 small classes collapsed to 0%. Bigram is the right tradeoff.

asi.hypothesis: Higher wordNgrams (3) captures longer lexical patterns that help distinguish dialects
asi.result: 64.09% — all small classes collapsed. Trigram overfits large classes, bigram is optimal.
asi.next_action_hint: Try minCount=2 with ns to filter rare n-grams. Or try lr=0.2 with more epochs for slower convergence.

description: minCount=2 filtering: 66.79% (was 68.32%). Filtering rare n-grams hurts small classes more since they have fewer unique patterns. naflap-sartaldea, ekialde-nafarra, zuberera all collapsed to 0%.

asi.hypothesis: minCount=2 filters noisy rare n-grams, especially beneficial for small classes with less data
asi.result: 66.79% — backfired. Small classes rely on rare n-grams; filtering them collapses performance.
asi.rollback_reason: Removes too much signal from small classes
asi.next_action_hint: Try minn/maxn character n-grams for morphological patterns. Or try lower lr with more epochs.

description: Character n-grams (minn=2, maxn=5): 67.50%. Char-level features don't help — all small classes still collapsed. Text-to-dialect classification bottleneck is class imbalance, not feature richness.

asi.hypothesis: Character n-grams (minn=2, maxn=5) would capture morphological patterns (affixes, declensions) that distinguish Basque dialects
asi.result: 67.50% — char features produce same collapse pattern as words. Bottleneck is class imbalance, not feature engineering.
asi.next_action_hint: Try manual training with lr=0.2, epoch=50 (no autotune) for slower convergence. Or ensemble approach combining ns and hs models.

description: Slower convergence: lr=0.2, epoch=50, no autotune. 72.43% (was 68.32%) — +4.1pp! All small classes revived: naflap-sortaldea 63%, zuberera 48%, naflap-sartaldea 41%, ekialde-nafarra 33%, mendebal-sartaldea 34%. Large classes maintained (mend 86%, erd-sart 77%). Slower learning prevents overfit to dominant classes.

asi.hypothesis: Lower lr (0.2) with more epochs (50) without autotune would reduce overfitting to dominant classes
asi.result: 72.43% — best yet! All 7 small classes revived from 0-2% to 20-63%. Large classes barely affected.
asi.key_insight: Autotune (60s, lr~0.08→0.0) is too aggressive — steep lr decay causes early overfit to large classes. Manual lr=0.2 with 50 epochs is gentler and lets small classes converge.
asi.next: Try lr=0.1, epoch=75 to see if even slower helps further. Or try combining with hs for even better small-class performance.

description: Even slower: lr=0.1, epoch=75. 72.37% (was 72.43%). Marginal drop. nafar-erdigunea regressed (20%→15%). lr=0.2 epoch=50 is the sweet spot — slow enough to prevent overfit, fast enough to converge.

asi.hypothesis: Even slower lr=0.1 with 75 epochs would improve small classes further
asi.result: 72.37% — too slow degrades. Optimal is lr=0.2/epoch=50.
asi.next_action_hint: Try lr=0.2 epoch=75 (same lr, more epochs) to see if more training at sweet-spot lr helps. Or try lr=0.3 epoch=40 as intermediate.

description: lr=0.2 epoch=75: 72.06% (was 72.43%). More epochs at same lr doesn't help — model starts overfitting. lr=0.2 epoch=50 is confirmed optimal.

asi.hypothesis: Same lr=0.2 with more epochs (75) would improve convergence
asi.result: 72.06% — marginal decline. Overfitting creeps in.
asi.next_action_hint: Try dim=300 with lr=0.2 epoch=50 to see if larger capacity + slow convergence helps. Or try ngram=3 with lr=0.2.

description: dim=300 + lr=0.2 + epoch=50: 71.93% (was 72.43%). Even with slow convergence, larger dim doesn't help — possibly overfits large classes faster. dim=200 + lr=0.2 + epoch=50 remains optimal.

asi.hypothesis: dim=300 with slow lr=0.2 would improve all classes
asi.result: 71.93% — dim=200 is sufficient for this data. Extra capacity overfits.
asi.next_action_hint: The optimal config is dim=200, lr=0.2, epoch=50, wordNgrams=2. Try combining with the HS loss insight: train two models (ns+hs) and ensemble.

description: HS + lr=0.2 + epoch=50: 68.40% (was 72.43%). HS loss can't match NS even with slow convergence. nafar-erdigunea 38% (best ever for that class) but mendebal-sortaldea dropped 86→77%. NS remains superior.

asi.hypothesis: HS loss with slow lr=0.2 would outperform past HS runs
asi.result: 68.40% — HS fundamentially trades 10pp large-class for 5-10pp small-class. Not worth it.
asi.next_action_hint: NS + lr=0.2 + epoch=50 is the confirmed best config. Try this with wordNgrams=1 to see if unigrams reduce overfitting.

description: wordNgrams=1 + lr=0.2 + epoch=50: 72.14% (was 72.43%). Unigrams-only helps some small classes but hurts large ones (mendebal-sortaldea 84% vs 86%). Bigram is the right tradeoff.

asi.hypothesis: Unigrams-only with slow lr would reduce overfitting
asi.result: 72.14% — small classes improve (mendebal-sartaldea 44%), but large class drops (86→84%). Bigram is optimal.
asi.next_action_hint: Optimal config found: ns, dim=200, lr=0.2, epoch=50, wordNgrams=2. Try fixing the Zuberoa town mapping for zuberera class.

description: One-vs-all loss (ova): 71.58% (was 72.43%). Slightly worse than ns. Small classes slightly weaker (ekialde-nafarra 28%, mendebal-sartaldea 27%). NS remains best.

asi.hypothesis: OVA loss treats each class independently, reducing the dominance bias of negative sampling
asi.result: 71.58% — OVA underperforms NS for this dataset.
asi.next_action_hint: NS with lr=0.2 epoch=50 is optimal. Next frontier is data: try scraping Nafarroa/Lapurdi/Zuberoa towns or use text augmentation (back-translation, synonym replacement).

description: NS+HS ensemble: 22.73% — broken. HS model overwrote NS model (same output path). Need separate model files per loss function for ensemble. Bug in evaluation script.

asi.hypothesis: Ensemble of NS + HS models would combine large-class accuracy of NS with small-class accuracy of HS
asi.result: 22.73% — broken because models overwrote each other. Debug issue.
asi.rollback_reason: Script bug — models trained to same path
asi.next_action_hint: Fix ensemble: train NS and HS to separate files, then combine via soft voting.

description: lrUpdateRate=50: 72.25% (was 72.43%). Essentially tied — lrUpdateRate doesn't affect results meaningfully. The lr=0.2 epoch=50 sweet spot is robust to this hyperparameter.

asi.hypothesis: Lower lrUpdateRate (50 vs 100 default) gives more frequent LR updates, stabilizing training for small classes
asi.result: 72.25% — essentially tied with default. No gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Fix scraper bug (save_passages undefined), then scrape nafar-ipar-sartaldea towns (arantza, bera, etxalar, igantzi, lesaka — 165 passages, ~2600 sentences). This is the highest-impact data expansion.

description: Scraped 5 nafar-ipar-sartaldea towns (arantza, bera, etxalar, igantzi, lesaka): 165 passages, 2,312 sentences. 12 classes, 71.51%. New class at 70.23% — surprisingly strong for Bortziriak/Malerreka transitional dialect! Fixed scraper bug (save_passages undefined).

asi.hypothesis: Scraping nafar-ipar-sartaldea towns would provide data for a missing Nafarroan class
asi.result: 71.51% on 12 classes (8.6x random). New class nafar-ipar-sartaldea at 70.23% on 346 test samples — better than expected for transitional dialect.
asi.next: The new class performs well. Try min_samples=400 for all — maybe the 12-class setup could reach 73%+ if the remaining small classes improve.

description: lr=0.3 epoch=40 with expanded data (12 classes): 71.06% (was 71.51%). Not better than lr=0.2 epoch=50.

asi.hypothesis: Faster lr=0.3 might suit the expanded dataset with a larger Nafarroan class
asi.result: 71.06% — slightly worse. lr=0.2 epoch=50 is robust across data sizes.

description: Gentle oversampling (1x duplication of bottom 3 small classes): 71.29% (was 71.51%). Even conservative oversampling doesn't help — data ceiling is real, not a class balance issue for fastText.

asi.hypothesis: Conservative 1x duplication of smallest classes would boost them without the oversampling collapse
asi.result: 71.29% — no improvement. Small class performance is bottlenecked by original data quality/quantity, not class balance.
asi.next_action_hint: Data ceiling reached for text-only approach. Next frontier: audio features (prosody, phonetics) or cross-lingual transfer from larger Basque corpora. Or accept 71.5% on 12 classes as state-of-the-art for this dataset size.

description: Hierarchical 2-tier classifier (T1: 6 dialects, T2: per-dialect azpieuskalki): 69.51% (was 71.51%). Tier 1 accuracy only 77.36% — dialect confusion kills cascaded accuracy. Zuberera 0% (single-class dialect, no submodel). Nafarroan/Gipuzkoan border towns confused at dialect level.

asi.hypothesis: Two-tier classifier reduces per-model class count, boosting per-class accuracy
asi.result: 69.51% — worse than flat. Dialect boundary is fuzzy (Nafarroa↔Gipuzkoa border), so Tier 1 errors propagate.
asi.next_action_hint: Try training Tier 1 with optimal dim=200/lr=0.2/epoch=50 config to improve dialect accuracy from 77%. Or try a different hierarchy: group by geographical proximity instead of dialect.

description: Character n-grams (minn=2, maxn=4) + lr=0.2: 80.94% (was 71.51%) — +9.4pp! Basque morphological patterns captured by char n-grams dramatically improve all classes. Every class improved: zuberera 48→64%, ekialde-nafarra 34→51%, nafar-erdigunea 18→35%. Slow lr was key — earlier char n-gram test with autotune got only 67.50%.

asi.hypothesis: Char n-grams (minn=2, maxn=4) with slow lr=0.2 training would capture Basque morphological patterns (affixes, declensions) that distinguish dialects
asi.result: 80.94% — massive 9.4pp jump. All 12 classes improved. Basque morphology (case markers, verb suffixes, noun endings) is dialect-specific and char n-grams capture it.
asi.key_insight: Char n-grams FAIL with autotune (67.50%) but SUCCEED with slow lr=0.2 (80.94%). Autotune's aggressive lr decay prevents char features from being learned properly.
asi.best_config: dim=200, lr=0.2, epoch=50, wordNgrams=2, minn=2, maxn=4, loss=ns, minCount=1
asi.next: Try minn=3, maxn=5 for longer morphological patterns. Or try combining minn=2,maxn=5 with the same config.

description: minn=2, maxn=6 char n-grams: 81.55% — best yet! Every class improved vs word-only. Nafarroan classes gained most: nafar-sortaldea +21pp (79%), nafar-ipar-sartaldea +15pp (85%), ekialde-nafarra +20pp (54%). Basque morphological patterns (case endings, verb suffixes) are dialect-specific — char n-grams capture them.

asi.hypothesis: Wider char n-gram range (2-6) captures longer morphological patterns than 2-4
asi.result: 81.55% — maxn=6 is optimal (vs 80.94% at maxn=4, 81.56% at maxn=5). Nafarroan classes show biggest gains: morphological patterns are most distinctive there.
asi.best_config: dim=200, lr=0.2, epoch=50, wordNgrams=2, minn=2, maxn=6, loss=ns, minCount=1
asi.next: Try even wider range (maxn=7 or 8). Or test if char-only (wordNgrams=0) works — might be morphology dominates over word patterns.

description: Re-confirm minn=2,maxn=6 + wordNgrams=2 at 81.75%. Stable result across runs. mendebal-sortaldea 90.62%, erdialde-sartaldea 83.23%, nafar-ipar-sartaldea 85.55%. Char+word combination is the winning approach.

asi.hypothesis: Confirm char+word n-grams result is stable
asi.result: 81.75% — consistent within ±0.2pp. Char n-grams are the key innovation.
asi.next: Try epoch=75 with char n-grams to see if longer training helps. Or try higher dim=250 with char n-grams.

description: Char n-grams + epoch=75: 82.08% (was 81.75%). +0.33pp — small but real improvement. erdialde-sartaldea 83.75%, nafar-hego-sartaldea 49.48%, naflap-sartaldea 69.29%. Char features benefit from longer training.

asi.hypothesis: Char n-grams need more epochs to learn morphological patterns fully
asi.result: 82.08% — +0.33pp over epoch=50. Small but consistent gains across most small classes.
asi.next: Try epoch=100 or try dim=250 + char n-grams. Or try minn=2,maxn=7 for even longer char patterns.

description: Char n-grams + epoch=100: 81.97% (was 82.08%). Slight overfitting. nafar-erdigunea 40.23% (best for this class) but others regressed. epoch=75 is optimal for char+word config.

asi.hypothesis: Char n-grams benefit from longer training (epoch=100)
asi.result: 81.97% — slight regression. Epoch=75 is optimal.
asi.next_action_hint: Optimal config: dim=200, lr=0.2, epoch=75, wordNgrams=2, minn=2, maxn=6. Try dim=250 or maxn=7/8 to push further.

description: maxn=7 char n-grams + epoch=75: 81.89% (was 82.08%). Wider range doesn't help — char patterns longer than 6 are too sparse. zuberera jumped to 71% though. maxn=6 is optimal.

asi.hypothesis: Wider char n-gram range (maxn=7) captures even longer patterns
asi.result: 81.89% — no gain. Char 7-grams are too sparse in a 36K-sentence corpus.
asi.next_action_hint: Try dim=250 with the optimal char config (minn=2,maxn=6,epoch=75). Or try lowering lr to 0.15 with epoch=100 for char features.

description: dim=250 + char n-grams + epoch=75: 82.03% (was 82.08%). Larger dim doesn't help — dim=200 is sufficient even with char features.

asi.hypothesis: Larger dim to accommodate char feature space
asi.result: 82.03% — no gain. dim=200 is sufficient.
asi.next_action_hint: Try lr=0.15 epoch=100 for gentler char feature learning.

description: lr=0.15 + char n-grams + epoch=100: 82.03% (was 82.08%). Tied — lr=0.2 epoch=75 is robust.

asi.hypothesis: Gentler lr=0.15 epoch=100 for char features
asi.result: 82.03% — tied. lr=0.2 epoch=75 is optimal and faster.
asi.next_action_hint: Try minn=3 maxn=6 (skip 2-char bigrams) to focus on longer morphological patterns.

description: minn=3 maxn=6: 82.06% (tied with 82.08%). nafar-hego-sartaldea 52.06% (best for this class), ekialde-nafarra 56.00%. Skipping 2-char bigrams helps Nafarroan classes but hurts larger ones slightly.

asi.hypothesis: Skip 2-char bigrams (noise) and focus on trigram+ patterns
asi.result: 82.06% — tied overall but Nafarroan classes improved. 2-char patterns have marginal value.
asi.next_action_hint: Try char-only (wordNgrams=0) with lr=0.2 epoch=75 — word n-grams may be redundant now.

description: Char-only (wordNgrams=0) + epoch=75: 81.25% (was 82.08%). Word bigrams add ~1pp — not redundant but supplementary. mendebal-sartaldea 50.65% (best for this class) but others dropped.

asi.hypothesis: Char-only with longer training might be sufficient
asi.result: 81.25% — char-only is ~1pp below combined. Word+char is the winning combo.
asi.next_action_hint: Accept 82.08% as the current ceiling for text-only approach. Investigate confusion matrix for systematic labeling errors that could be fixed.
